name: photo-color
desc: Free, open-source photo colorizer for Windows — bring black-and-white shots to life locally, batch albums. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **One-click colorize** — grayscale photos get natural color from a local model in seconds
✅ **Palette nudges** — warmth, saturation and skin tone sliders fix the AI's odd choices
✅ **Batch album mode** — 300 family scans colorized with consistent settings
✅ **Saturation limiter** — stops the candy-color look that plagues automatic colorizers
✅ **Split view** — draggable divider between original and colorized at matching zoom
✅ **Sidecar settings** — every output remembers which sliders produced it, reproducible later
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, models download separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Feature | **photo-color** | DeOldify scripts | MyHeritage | Photoshop colorize |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Paid | Subscription |
| Photos stay local | **Yes** | Yes | Upload | Yes
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Python env plus GPU setup | Browser | Installer
faqQ: how to colorize old black and white photos free on Windows?
faqA: The open colorizer is a research repo with GPU setup pain, and the friendly services upload your family photos and bill per image. photo-color runs local models, tames saturation and colorizes whole albums in batch. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline.
s1: Dark studio (#121418, rose #F43F5E): split divider over a colorized wedding portrait, saturation limiter dial at 0.5, warmth and skin tone sliders below.
s2: Batch album: 300 scans with thumbnails filling in colorized, consistent settings locked badge, progress at 61 percent, ETA chip.
s3: Settings history: sidecar card listing last export with all slider values, reopen settings action, before and after strip at the bottom.
